channel.title: Nature Communications
channel.description:
Nature Communications is an open access, multidisciplinary journal dedicated to publishing high-quality research in all areas of the biological, health, physical, chemical and Earth sciences. Papers published by the journal aim to represent important advances of significance to specialists within each field.

We are committed to providing an efficient service for both authors and readers. Our team of independent editors make rapid and fair publication decisions. Prompt dissemination of accepted papers to a wide readership and beyond is achieved through a programme of continuous online publication.

item.title: Anti-Kasha fluorescence and persistent room-temperature phosphorescence from a nearly flat non-symmetric polycyclic hydrocarbon
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 02 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78107-6

Polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbons are efficient emitters, but achieving desirable properties can be challenging. Here, the authors report the development of monohomotruxene, a nonsymmetric compound with anti-kasha and ultra-long blue phosphorescence.
item.dc:title: Anti-Kasha fluorescence and persistent room-temperature phosphorescence from a nearly flat non-symmetric polycyclic hydrocarbon

item.title: Different concentrations of atropine in children with high myopia: a 2-year multicenter double-blind, randomized controlled trial
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 02 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77797-2

Here the authors report the results of a multicenter, double-blind, randomized-controlled trial that evaluates the effect and safety of different concentration atropine eyedrops (0.01%, 0.04%, 0.10%) for myopia control in children with high myopia. The findings show that nightly use of 0.10% atropine eye drops for 24 months mitigated myopia progression with an acceptable safety profile.
item.dc:title: Different concentrations of atropine in children with high myopia: a 2-year multicenter double-blind, randomized controlled trial

item.title: Molecularly engineered zwitterionic‑fluorinated hydrogel electrolyte for durable Ah-level zinc-ion batteries
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 01 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-77562-5

Aqueous zinc-ion batteries promise safe energy storage but suffer from dendrites and side reactions. Here, authors engineer a zwitterionic fluorinated hydrogel electrolyte to suppress these issues, enabling durable, dendrite free, Ah-level pouch cells.
item.dc:title: Molecularly engineered zwitterionic‑fluorinated hydrogel electrolyte for durable Ah-level zinc-ion batteries

item.title: Repurposing the evolutionary fitness of marine bacteria for water-conserving conversion of lignin-derived carbon
item.content:encoded:
Nature Communications, Published online: 01 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41467-026-78209-1

Reverting waste carbon into chemicals with minimal freshwater use is essential for a sustainable future. Here, the authors engineer the marine bacterium R. nubinhibens, by decoupling bioproduction from central metabolism to convert lignin into chemicals with seawater as a water source.
item.dc:title: Repurposing the evolutionary fitness of marine bacteria for water-conserving conversion of lignin-derived carbon
